# Framework Scaffolding

## Folder structure

Always generate into the layout matched from `config/frameworks/folder-structure/`
for the framework/language named in `autopilot-ui/configs/new/config.json`.
Don't default to a generic layout, and don't invent a new one even if it
looks cleaner - consistency across every generated project is the point,
since the same reviewer, the same CI job, and the same stabilizer agent all
assume that shape.

## Logging - log4j by default

Every generated framework wires up log4j and logs every meaningful event by
default: navigation, every action performed on a locator, every assertion
(pass and fail), and any retry. This is not optional per-project
configuration - it's how failures get diagnosed later without re-running in
headed mode every time.

Minimum logging shape:

- One logger per Page Object / module, named after the class.
- INFO for actions taken (`"Clicked LoginButtonSubmit"`).
- WARN for a fallback locator strategy being used instead of the primary one.
- ERROR for a failed action, including the locator key and the strategy that
  was tried.
- Log output goes to both console and a rolling file under a project-standard
  logs directory, so CI can archive it as a build artifact.

## Environment configuration, never hardcoded values

- Base URLs, credentials, timeouts, and anything else that differs by
  environment come from `config/environments/<env>.env.json` - never
  hardcoded in generated source.
- Generated code reads the environment name from a single place (an env var
  or CLI flag), not scattered across files, so switching environments is a
  one-line change.
- No credential - not even a "test" one - is ever written as a literal
  string in generated code. If a credential is needed for local development,
  generate a `.env.example` entry, not a real value.

## Test data

Generate test data in the format specified by
`autopilot-ui/configs/new/config.json`. Do not default to a different shape
(for example, don't switch to inline fixtures if the config specifies
external JSON files) - the config is the source of truth for this project's
test-data convention, not a suggestion.

## Learned patterns

Read [references/learned-patterns.md](./references/learned-patterns.md) when handling test data and environment values. It holds test-data fixes engineers made by hand: values moved to environment variables, guards for missing data - fixes that recurred across several files and engineers and were approved by a reviewer (generated by `npm run learn-publish`; do not edit it by hand). Treat it as part of this skill.

If you hit a problem it does not cover, run `npm run lookup-fix -- "<problem>"`. After you fix it by hand, record the fix with `npm run learn-capture -- --worktree --write --why "<what was wrong>"` so it can become a pattern (see the **fix-knowledge-base** skill).
